challenges.title: Passage 1: Hunan Dishes and Culture
challenges.summary: 本文是一篇说明文。湘菜以辛辣的味道而闻名，本文主要介绍了湘菜的历史，湖南人爱吃辣的原因及其与湖南人的性格的关系。
passage: Talking about Hunan Province, what comes to your mind first?
Unquestionably, most answers are Hunan dishes, which are called Xiang dishes.
Hunan dishes, with a history of more than two thousand years, are famous for their spicy taste.
It is one of China's eight great cuisines.
Chili peppers(辣椒) are the most important and popular part of Hunan dishes.
They were introduced from South America in the late 1580s.
Since then, they have won the hearts of Hunan people.
While Sichuan dishes are famous for their classic numbing and hot(麻辣) taste, Hunan dishes are known for being "hot".
Hunan people invented many ways to cook chili peppers.
For example, they cut fresh chili peppers into small pieces and mix them with salt, and they use the chopped pepper(剁椒) to steam (蒸) fish heads.
Then it has become a classic dish around the world.
Some say Hunan people love chilies because they can help people get used to the damp(潮湿的) weather.
The chili can drive away the dampness in one's body.
Chili has now become a part of Hunan culture.
It is believed that the chili and the personality(个性) of Hunan people have something in common.
Usually described as direct, brave and hard-working, Hunan people are famous for their "hot personalities".
It is clear that they would fall in love with chili peppers.

passage_cn: 说到湖南省，你首先想到的是什么？
毫无疑问，大多数人的回答都是湖南菜，也就是我们常说的湘菜。
湘菜有着两千多年的历史，以辣味闻名。
它是中国八大菜系之一。
辣椒是湖南菜中最重要、最受欢迎的元素。
它们是在16世纪80年代末从南美洲引入的。
从那时起，它们就赢得了湖南人民的心。
如果说四川菜以其独特的麻辣风味闻名，那么湖南菜则以“纯辣”著称。
湖南人发明了许多烹饪辣椒的方法。
例如，他们把新鲜辣椒切碎并加上盐腌制，然后用这种剁椒来蒸鱼头。
这道菜后来成为了风靡全球的经典名菜。
有人说湖南人爱吃辣椒是因为辣椒能帮助人们适应潮湿的天气。
辣椒能够驱散人体内的湿气。
如今，辣椒已经成为了湖南文化的一部分。
人们认为辣椒和湖南人的性格有相通之处。
湖南人通常被形容为直爽、勇敢和勤劳，他们以“火辣的性格”而闻名。
很显然，他们爱上辣椒是顺理成章的事。

challenges.title: Passage 2: Xian Xinghai
challenges.summary: 本文介绍了中国著名音乐家冼星海的生平经历、音乐成就以及他的代表作。
passage: Xian Xinghai was a very famous musician in China.
He wrote one of the greatest pieces of music of the 20th century.
In his short life he wrote nearly 300 songs and an opera.
Xian was born in Macao in 1905.
Because his father died before he was born, Xian had to move from place to place with his mother.
He began learning to play the violin when he was 20 years old.
At the beginning, his violin was so cheap and of poor quality that he could not play it well.
His friends laughed at him.
Xian did not stop practicing and soon showed his talent.
In 1929, he became the first Chinese student who studied in a special music school in Paris.
Before he left, Xian became the school's best student and won several prizes for his talents.
In 1935, he returned to China and helped fight against the Japanese army.
Later, he went to Yan'an to teach music at a college.
Although there were no pianos in Yan'an at that time, Xian still wrote some of his most important music there, including Yellow River Cantata, one of his most famous works.
In May 1940, Xian was sent to the Soviet Union by the Chinese Communist Party to write music for a documentary.
In the Soviet Union, life was very hard.
Xian got sick and later he died of a lung illness on October 30, 1945, aged only 40.
Xian Xinghai is such a great man and his music will live on in people's hearts forever.

passage_cn: 洑星海是中国非常有名的音乐家。
他写出了20世纪最伟大的音乐作品之一。
在他短曨的一生中，他写了近300首歌曲和一部歌剧。
洑星海1905年出生于澳门。
因为他父亲在他出生前就去世了，洑星海不得不和母亲一起拥过着拨涛洞家、淋雨食食的浪艙生活。
他20岁时开始学尚尺小提琢。
初学时，他的小提琴很便宜且质量很差，以致于他无法开山生次。
他的朋友们都反笑他。
洑星海沢有停止练琴，不久便展露出了他的天赋。
1929年，他成为第一位在巴黎一所特笑音乐学校学习的中国学生。
在他离开前，洑星海已经成为该校最优秀的学生，并出个才华赢得了几项奖项。
1935年，他回到中国，并参与抗日斑争。
后来，他去了延安的一所大学教授音乐。
尽管当时延安沢有钢琴，但洑星海仍然在那里写了一些他最重要的音乐作品，其中就包括他最著名的作品之一——《黄河大合唱》。
1940年5月，洑星海被中国共产党派往苏联，为一部纪录片配乐。
在苏联，生活非常艰辛。
洑星海生了病，并于1945年10月30日因肺病去世，去年仅40岁。
洑星海是如此伟大的一位人物，他的音乐将永远活在人们的心中。

challenges.title: Passage 3: US-China Student Exchange Journey
challenges.summary: 本文是一篇记叙文。在一个长达八天的中美交流活动中，两国的学生加深了对彼此的文化的了解。
passage: There is a big difference between knowing another country from social media and experiencing it in person.
This is what students from the US and China discovered during an eight-day exchange journey.
From March 24 to 31, a group of 15 students from the US went on an educational and cultural exchange in China.
For Micheal, a 15-year-old 10th grader, this was his first time going abroad.
While in Beijing, Micheal bravely tried douzhi, a fermented(发酵的) bean juice.
It is a challenge even for locals.
However, he finished three bowls in a row.
Besides Chinese food, Micheal also likes Chinese people because he thinks they are welcoming and open-minded.
"I tried out table tennis after classes ended, and the Chinese students played like professionals," he said.
"In the United States, students usually do sports through clubs and sports teams.
Sports are more for fun here."
The learning was two-sided.

Li Weiyou, a 15-year-old student from Beijing No. 4 High School International Campus and also Micheal's homestay partner, said, "Before I knew Micheal, I thought US students paid more attention to personal development than schoolwork.
But to my surprise, Micheal does well in both," Li said.
With technology and media developing quickly, teenagers can get information about other countries online easily.
However, online searches show only a tiny part of the full story of cultural exchange.
"If I hadn't taken this trip, I wouldn't have learned about the high school life of Chinese students," said Micheal.
For Micheal, the week-long trip even influenced his further aspirations(抱负).
"I used to consider becoming a math teacher in the United States.
Now, I'm dreaming about teaching English in Beijing or Shanghai in the near future."

passage_cn: 从社交媒体上了解另一个国家与亲身体验它有着巨大的区别。
这是中美两国的学生在一次为期八天的交流之旅中发现的。
3月24日至31日，来自美国的15名学生前往中国进行了一次教育与文化交流。
对于15岁的高一学生米歇尔（Micheal）来说，这是他第一次出国。
在北京期间，米歇尔勇敢地尝试了豆汁——一种发酵豆汁。
这对当地人来说都是一个挑战。
然而，他一口气喝了三碗。
除了中国美食，米歇尔还喜欢中国人民，因为他觉得他们热情好客、思想开放。
“课后我尝试了乒乓球，中国学生打得就像专业选手一样，”他说。
在美国，学生通常通过俱乐部和运动队来参加体育活动。
这里的体育运动更多是为了好玩。
这种学习是双向的。
北京四中国际校区15岁的学生、同时也是米歇尔寄宿家庭伙伴的李维友（Li Weiyou，音译）说：“在认识米歇尔之前，我以为美国学生比学业更注重个人发展。”
“但令我惊讶的是，米歇尔在学业和个人发展两方面都表现得很出色，”李说。
随着科技和媒体的飞速发展，青少年可以很容易地在网上获取关于其他国家的信息。
然而，网络搜索只能展现文化交流全貌的冰山一角。
米歇尔说：“如果我没有参加这次旅行，我就不会了解到中国学生的高中生活。”
对米歇尔来说，这为期一周的旅行甚至影响了他未来的志向。
“我过去曾考虑在美国当一名数学老师。
现在，我梦想着在不久的将来能在北京或上海教英语。”

challenges.summary: 本文是一篇说明文。文章主要介绍了位于瑞士苏黎世的世界最大巧克力博物馆——瑞士莲巧克力之家。
passage: Do you have a sweet tooth?
Are you a fan of chocolate?
If you are answering "yes" to both of these questions, then the Lindt Home of Chocolate should be a good place for you to go.
The Lindt Home of Chocolate is the world's largest chocolate museum.
It is in Zurich, Switzerland.
It was first opened to the public in September 2020.
If you are looking to take some great photos at the museum, look no further than the chocolate fountain (喷泉).
The fountain is over nine meters high.
Around 1,500 kilograms of melted(融化的)chocolate is flowing through it.
To the disappointment of chocolate lovers, they can enjoy the fountain but they are not allowed to put their hands into it.
In addition to the fountain, the museum offers many other things.
The exhibitions(展览) introduce the history of chocolate to visitors.
Along the way, there are plenty of tasting chances.
The museum even has a space for chocolate-making classes.
Visitors can learn to design and make their own chocolate there.
Switzerland is known for its high-quality chocolate.
In the eyes of the Swiss, this tasty brown food stands as a national pride.
Almost everyone in the country takes chocolate seriously.
The Lindt Home of Chocolate is expected to spread the love for chocolate.

challenges.title: Passage 5: Rain Water (Yushui)
challenges.summary: 本文是一篇说明文，主要介绍了二十四节气中的“雨水”，包括其自然特点、传统习俗以及生活建议。
passage: In China, the 24 solar terms(节气) were created thousands of years ago to guide farmers to work better.
They also reflect China's rich history through seasonal festivals, special food, cultural activities, family gatherings and even healthy living tips of each solar term.
Rain Water or Yushui is a symbol of the increase in rainfall and rise in temperature.
With its arrival, <u>grass and trees turn green again</u>.
This year, Rain Water starts on Feb. 19 and ends on Mar. 4.
There is an ancient Chinese saying, <u>"Rain during the springtime is as valuable as oil,"</u> showing the importance of rain to plants and farming.
Around this period, the most important thing for the farmers is timely irrigation(灌溉), especially in northern China where rainfall is less.
It is an ancient Chinese tradition for married daughters to pay a visit to their parents during the day of Yushui.

The traditional gifts are a piece of red silk which expresses the best wishes for the parents to have good health and a pot of stewed (炖) meat that shows their respect and gratitude (感激) to the parents for raising them as children.
And this tradition is kept alive in many areas across China.

challenges.title: Passage 11: The Carbon Passport
challenges.summary: 本文是一篇说明文，主要介绍为了减少碳排放，一个旅游公司建议使用“碳护照”，很多国家也纷纷采取行动去减少航空旅行。
passage: The summer of 2023 saw record-breaking heatwaves across many parts of the world.
As temperatures continue to rise, the effect of carbon emissions(碳排放) on the environment has become a big problem.
Studies show the travel industry is responsible for about 10% of these emissions, with air travel alone causing about 2.8% of them.
To address this problem, Intrepid-a travel company, has suggested a "carbon passport" in its recent report.
The idea behind it is that each traveler would have a yearly carbon limit, and nobody can go over that limit.
Using carbon passports means travelers will have to take fewer flights to lower their "carbon footprint" the CO2 emissions from their actions.
At present, the carbon footprint of each person is about four tons yearly on average (平均).
To limit temperature rise to acceptable levels by 2050, our goal should be below two tons.
In line with this goal, some European countries are taking steps to reduce air travel.
In France, local flights are canceled if the same trips can be made by train in 2.5 hours or less.
In Belgium, additional charges (收费) are added to short-distance flights to encourage other forms of travel.
Intrepid considers the idea of a "carbon passport" effective with more people involved in.
Travelers will receive information about their carbon footprints and change their travel habits.
And businesses will be pushed to use more green practices.
Alex Hawkins, one of the writers of the report, says, "These passports will make us think more about how our trips influence the environment."
When it comes to monitoring everyone's carbon emission, Anna Abelson, a professor of the New York University thinks it would be a challenge in terms of logistics (统计).
Even if we work that out, there are still some worries.
For example, people might not be able to take jobs far away or visit family in other cities as often.
Some even worry about privacy and personal freedom if we start monitoring and limiting people's air travel.
"Getting everyone on board with carbon passports won't be easy," Hawkins added.
"It would need support from lots of different people and groups all over the world."
However, even with the challenges, the idea of carbon passports shows the need for us to take action together to fight climate change and make travel eco-friendlier.

passage_cn: 2023年夏天，世界许多地方都遭遇了破纪录的热浪。
随着气温持续攀升，碳排放对环境的影响已经成了一个大问题。
研究表明，旅游业约占这些碳排放的10%，其中仅航空旅行就造成了约2.8%的排放。
为了解决这个问题，旅游公司Intrepid在其最近的一份报告中提出了“碳护照”的概念。
这一构想背后的思路是，每个旅客每年都有一个碳排放额度，任何人不得超过该限额。
使用碳护照意味着旅客将不得不减少乘机次数，以降低他们的碳足迹——即他们的行为所产生的二氧化碳排放量。
目前，每个人每年的碳足迹平均约为4吨。
为了到2050年将气温升幅限制在可接受的水平，我们的目标应当降至2吨以下。
为契合这一目标，一些欧洲国家正采取措施减少航空旅行。
在法国，如果同样的行程坐火车能在2小时半或更短时间内到达，当地航班就会被取消。
在比利时，短途航班会被加收额外费用，以鼓励人们选择其他出行方式。
Intrepid认为，如果有更多人参与进来，“碳护照”的构想将会十分奏效。
旅客将获得有关自身碳足迹的信息，并借此改变旅行习惯。
同时，企业也将被推动去采用更多环保做法。
该报告的作者之一亚历克斯·霍金斯（Alex Hawkins）表示：“这些护照将让我们更多地思考我们的出行是如何影响环境的。”
谈到监测每个人的碳排放时，纽约大学教授安娜·阿贝尔森（Anna Abelson）认为这在后勤管理上将是一个挑战。
即便我们解决了这个问题，依然存在一些担忧。
例如，人们可能无法再去远处工作，或者不能像以前那样频繁地去外地探亲。
还有人担心，如果我们开始监测并限制人们的航空旅行，会侵犯隐私和个人自由。
霍金斯补充说：“要让所有人支持‘碳护照’并非易事。”
“这需要世界各地许多不同人员和群体的支持。”
然而，尽管面临种种挑战，“碳护照”的构想依然表明，我们需要共同采取行动来对抗气候变化，并让旅行变得更加环保。

challenges.title: Passage 13: Reading with The Fingertips
challenges.summary: 本文讲述了路易·布莱叶（Louis Braille）的生平经历以及他和查尔斯·巴比耶（Charles Barbier）共同改良盲文的发明故事。
passage: Louis Braille was born in France in 1809.
When he was three, he injured an eye in an accident in his father's workshop.
The infection (感染) from the wound spread to his other eye.
Within a year he couldn't see anything.
When he was ten, he was sent to a school for the blind.
Students there learned by listening to their teachers.
One day, a visitor came to the school.
His name was Charles Barbier.
He was to have a great influence on Braille.
Louis was then twelve years old.
Barbier had invented a new way of writing.
He had hoped the French army would adopt (采纳) his method.
This writing was designed to be used at night.
Soldiers could read it without showing a light.
Barbier hoped the head of the school whose students lived their lives in darkness could use his way of writing.
Louis Braille stood out among those students.
His mind was quick.
He was eager to learn.
The head of school invited him to meet the visitor.
Barbier began to show how his writing worked.
Braille's interest was aroused.
Barbier took a sheet of thick paper.
Using a pointed instrument, he punched a series of holes to make raised dots (点) on the other side of the paper.
These dots were grouped together in cells (单元格).
The cells could be placed in any of twelve positions.
Each group stood for a different sound.
By running a fingertip over them, a person could read a message.
Braille was excited by Barbier's invention.
But he knew that it needed to be simpler.
He started working on it at once.
Instead of twelve positions for each unit, he decided to work with six.
This let a reader make sense of the raised dots more quickly and easily.
Braille remained at the school all his life, He taught there.
He also helped to print books that used his method.
Braille was a very good musician.
He showed people how to write music in his way.
Charles Barbier did not sell his method to the army.
But he played a part in changing forever the way blind people read.
Because of what he started and Louis Braille completed, people everywhere who cannot see are no longer limited by blindness.
